automationStories.title: UCSB Data Science Club Payment Confirmation Script
automationStories.description: Previously, we had to split the payment verification screenshots of 500 members across 15 officers. I made a Google Apps Script automation that used the Gmail API to track incoming Zelle payment emails and extract the sender's name. Unfortunately, there wasn't a good way to get their email so I used their name like a foreign key to query our member spreadsheet with the Sheets API to retrieve their email that they registered with. Then, it would send them a confirmation email that they use to verify club membership at our general meetings. This saved us officers each 30 minutes across Fall and Winter quarters. We do this every year so these 30 minutes can be spent doing something else of interest :)

automationStories.title: UCSB Engineering Student Council Attendance Tracker
automationStories.description: As the secretary, my task was to log attendance from each meeting minutes document of the quarter into a large spreadsheet. I slacked on this for almost a year because I was afraid of the tedious work. To solve this, I created a Google Apps Script automation that used the Docs API to fetch attendance info and integrated with the Sheets API to log the entries, saving me 30 min every quarter. To pass the torch, I wrote a small document for a future ESC member to push run which auto-populates the attendance tracker sheet for simplicity.

automationStories.title: Amazon Alexa Widget Development Script
automationStories.description: Due to confidentiality reasons I can't reveal the exact process, but it's like: run command 1 to generate id1, use id1 to run command 2 to get id2, use id1 and id2 to get id3, check status of id3 to see fail/success after 3 minutes. In the short term, it saved me just maybe 5-10 minutes every day. But because we develop our widgets often, this saves hours in the long run where I can work more on other tasks with the time I saved.

projects.title: FacEmotion
projects.description: An exploration of how a curious technical question becomes a real computer-vision pipeline.
projects.question: How can visual signals become a useful, understandable emotion-classification experience?
projects.approach: Built from the model outward—connecting practical computer vision work to a concrete product-shaped implementation.

projects.title: MoodMap
projects.description: A real-time community mood map where people can share how they feel, discover the atmosphere around them, and help keep the space constructive.
projects.question: How might a shared emotional map feel open and expressive while still giving the community meaningful moderation tools?
projects.approach: Combined a map-first React experience with a FastAPI backend, Supabase authentication, and progressive moderation rules.

projects.title: YOLO Scooter Pathfinding
projects.description: A prototype that turns a monocular video feed into clear, real-time scooter guidance around obstacles.
projects.question: How can live object detection become a practical, safer path and speed suggestion for a rider?
projects.approach: Paired YOLO detection and tracking with obstacle inflation, motion-aware risk scoring, open-gap planning, and an optional live phone dashboard.

projects.title: GitPromptChain
